title: Pulse iteration scorecard (personal)
body:
Pulse iteration scorecard — personal scratch sheet

Context:
Quick personal tracker for small-batch inference experiments (prompt prefixes, KV cache, quant, batching). Meant to capture runs I want to triage into a proper bench job. Not official results — rough numbers from local dedicated pool.

Snapshot table (TSV — columns: run_id, date, epoch, prompt_variant, batch, kv_cache_hit_rate, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1k_usd, qa_f1):
R-031	2026-03-01	1	short-instr	8	0.12	18	42	220	0.032	0.82
R-032	2026-03-02	1	short-instr + warm_prefix	8	0.68	14	30	370	0.025	0.81
R-033	2026-03-03	1	short-instr + int8	8	0.15	15	33	330	0.021	0.79
R-034	2026-03-04	1	short-instr + warm_prefix + int8	8	0.71	12	28	520	0.018	0.77
R-035	2026-03-05	2	long-instr	4	0.05	28	65	120	0.048	0.86
R-036	2026-03-06	2	long-instr + cache	4	0.58	20	50	240	0.035	0.85
R-037	2026-03-07	2	long-instr + cache + 4-bit	4	0.54	19	49	260	0.028	0.83
R-038	2026-03-08	2	long-instr + cache + 4-bit + batching=16	16	0.55	22	52	420	0.019	0.82

Quick takeaways:
- Warm prefix caching has the largest R/O: hit rate jump -> tokens/s +~70% in short-instr runs (R-032 vs R-031).
- Quantization (int8/4-bit) reduces per-token cost notably; mixed impact on QA F1 (see R-033 and R-037).
- Batch=16 helps throughput but pushes p50 up slightly for long-instr; good for background/off-peak workloads.
- For production-facing QA tasks we need to gate quantization with regression checks (threshold: delta F1 >= -0.02 triggers rollback).

Rough cost scaling formula I use here for quick estimates:
- base_cost_per_1k = cost_per_1k_usd measured above (use run row)
- est_monthly_cost_usd = base_cost_per_1k * (avg_tokens_per_request * qps * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30) / 1000
(keep in mind cache reduces avg_tokens_per_request depending on hit rate)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need to measure cold vs warm KV cache hit ramp (0->100 requests) — is latency improvement stable after 30s of steady traffic?
- Where is SDK trace flag to tag a run with "cache_warm"? Add as default tag in local harness.
- Why did 4-bit (R-037) preserve QA F1 better than int8 (R-033)? Hypothesis: different quant path + kernel selection; re-run with deterministic seeds and eval set.

Next actions (short):
- [ ] Create Linear ticket with R-032/R-034 artifacts and request canary 4h soak (owner: me) -> Linear: RED-1023
- [ ] Add regression check to bench harness: require F1 >= baseline - 0.02 for quant runs (owner: Zoe)
- [ ] Schedule 24h soak with batch=4 + cache for long-instr workload (owner: Anika)
- [ ] Create small PR to emit sdk.trace_tags: ["cache_warm","quant:int8"] (PR drafted -> see linked GH)

Handy snippets / commands I used:
- run harness: python tools/bench/run_local.py --model llama-13b --batch 8 --quant int8 --prefix-cache=enabled --out results/R-033.json
- quick parse: cat results/R-033.json | jq '{p50:.metrics.p50, p95:.metrics.p95, tps:.metrics.tokens_per_sec}'

Notes for later write-up:
- If warm-prefix caching shows consistent >0.6 hit rate across customer prompt patterns, propose adding a default caching hint to the SDK (opt-in flag for hosted plans).
- Collect 10k eval prompts and run A/B on quant vs fp16 with deterministic seeding before any Dedicated rollout.

Personal log: ran R-034 overnight, saw steady hit rate 0.7 and tokens/s ~520 for ~6h window. Will extract traces tomorrow and attach to Linear ticket.

-- Morris
